marketOrderTooltip: A market order buys or sells {{asset}} immediately at the best available price based on the liquidity in the orderbook.
limitOrderTooltip:
A limit order lets you buy or sell {{asset}} at a specific price or better. Your order will only execute if the market reaches your chosen price.

Example: if the asset is trading at $100, you can place a buy order at $95 and wait for the market to reach that price before the trade executes.
trackingOrderTooltip:
A tracking order follows the market price and automatically updates your order at a set discount or premium. This can help you catch sharp price drops when buying, strong price spikes when selling, or execute larger trades while limiting price impact.

Example: if {{asset}} is $100 and you set a -2% deviation, your buy order stays 2% below the market price as it moves. If the market suddenly drops because of a large sell or liquidation, your order automatically updates and can help you buy at a discount.

You can also use tracking orders for larger trades. For example, setting a sell order with a +0.3% deviation can help you sell near the oracle price while giving arbitrageurs an incentive to fill your order quickly.
recurringOrderTooltip:
A recurring swap automatically buys or sells assets at regular intervals over time. This can help reduce the impact of short-term price movements by spreading trades across multiple executions.

Example: instead of buying $1,000 of {{asset}} at once, you can split it into 10 daily swaps of $100 each within your chosen price settings.

skewSizeTooltip1: A 1.0x skew spreads capital evenly across all orders.
skewSizeTooltip2: A 2.0x skew places larger orders closer to $100.
skewSizeTooltip3: A 0.5x skew places larger orders closer to $80.

scaleOrderTooltip:
A scale order creates multiple limit orders at once between your chosen start and end prices. This helps spread your trade across a price range instead of relying on a single entry or exit price.

Example: if {{asset}} is $100 and you want to buy between $90 and $80, a scale order can automatically place multiple smaller buy orders across that range. As the market moves down, each order will fill at its set price.
customConcentratedLiquidityTooltip:
Custom Concentrated Liquidity lets you choose the price range where your liquidity is active. Concentrating liquidity into a smaller range can increase trading fee generation while the market trades within that range.

For example, if BTC is trading at $100,000, you could set a range between $90,000 and $110,000. Your position earns fees while BTC stays inside that range. If the price moves outside the range, your position stops earning fees until the market returns.

When setting your range, make sure you are comfortable with the average buy price below your Low range and the average sell price above your High range.
rangePresetSelectionTooltip:
You can choose from several preset strategies or build your own. Different options work better depending on market conditions, your goals, and your preferred level of risk.

Custom Strategy gives you more control and lets you tailor the strategy to your preferences. Use the settings below to configure your range, spread, skew, and yield distribution.
rangePresetPassiveTooltip: Good for long-term “set and forget” liquidity. Covers a very wide range and stays active through large market moves, but usually earns lower fees than tighter ranges. Mostly suited for long-term liquidity that should remain active even during extreme volatility.
rangePresetWideTooltip: Good for volatile assets. Balances fee generation and range coverage while reducing the chance of moving out of range too quickly.
rangePresetTightTooltip: Best for stablecoins or low-volatility pairs. Concentrates liquidity close to the current price to maximize fee generation, but the position can leave the range more easily.
rangePresetLowerTooltip: Useful if you want to accumulate more of {{base}} as the price falls. The strategy gradually buys more of the asset as the market moves down while also earning you fees. If the market falls below your range, the position becomes fully converted into {{base}} and stops earning fees until the price moves back into range.
rangePresetHigherTooltip: Useful if you want to gradually sell into strength as the price rises. The strategy converts more of your position into the {{quote}} asset as the market moves up while also earning you fees. If the market rises above your range, the position becomes fully converted into the {{quote}} asset and stops earning fees until the price moves back into range.
rangePresetCopyTooltip: Lets you mirror the settings of a top-performing position. Useful if you want guidance from existing successful strategies.
avgBuyPriceTooltip:
Estimated average {{base}} purchase price if the market moves below your selected range.

Example: if your range is between {{lowRange}} and {{highRange}}, this shows the estimated average price you would pay for {{base}} if the market falls below {{lowRange}} and your position becomes fully converted into {{base}}.
avgSellPriceTooltip:
Estimated average {{base}} sale price if the market moves above your selected range.

Example: if your range is between {{lowRange}} and {{highRange}}, this shows the estimated average price you would receive for {{base}} if the market rises above {{highRange}} and your position becomes fully converted into {{quote}}.
